title: Operator-authorized creative design supplement: internal conversion and network defects
question: Can creative construction complement the completed literature audit with an explicitly hypothetical, cheaply rejectable mechanism addressing the actual TECT missing inputs?
method: Treat the operator's new instruction as authorization for a design review, not new model adoption or reopening the frozen two-source calculation.
Compare an internal-conversion parent aimed at R158 control provenance with a same-variable graph order/defect concept.
Use separate read-only reviewers to expose symmetry, exchange, Hessian, zero-state, memory, clustering and hidden-background obligations.
Preserve the two sketches as IDEA008/009 with one preferred admission question and no simulation, external-source expansion, theorem claim or automatic successor.
finding: Creative construction need not wait for a finished literature owner, but its new assumptions must remain explicit. Internal conversion is the preferred design question because it directly targets R158's missing physical control law; its added coupling cannot be assumed to preserve the old Hessian or state dynamics. The graph design is a reserve idea with weak theorem reuse and a dense-block competitor test. Neither is an adopted physical candidate or completed minimum model.
decision_reason: This is durable hypothesis generation and critical design support requested during checkpoint completion. It does not close the active gate or certify the illustrative equations as a physical law.
boundary: No new verifier/Lean execution, numerical result, theorem, model adoption or physical promotion for either sketch. PHY002 source-local runs do not validate them. No original P1/PAH changes, physical Pre-A, spacetime, QFT, gravity, continuum or TOE.
next_action: After a separate minimum-model admission only, audit one closed-conversion symmetry/exchange/Hessian contract without fitted mu(t) or rescuing terms. No automatic follow-on calculation.
